commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Vite migration baseline re-measured on the testing-library majors
details: The migration plan asked for a re-measurement if more dependency work landed before phase 1, and the testing-library major did land. Still 16 suites and 257 tests, now measured on top of jest-dom 7.0.1 and user-event 14.6.5. The major was taken deliberately before phase 1 rather than during it, because it changes the instrument the migration is measured with.

Records how that measurement nearly went wrong. npm install reported "up to date" while node_modules still held the old versions -- npm had written the new ones into its hidden lockfile without replacing the package directories. A run against that tree would have reported a green 257 measured on the old testing-library and declared the majors safe on no evidence. CI is immune because it installs with npm ci on a clean runner; local runs are not.

Adds removing @testing-library/user-event to the cleanup phase. Zero files import it -- it arrived with the Create React App template and was never used, which is why a 13 to 14 major was a no-op here despite v14 being the release that made the API async.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Vite migration plan refreshed against a moved acc
details: The plan was written on 29 August and reviewed 34 commits later. Its phases are unchanged; what changed is the ground it described. The acceptance baseline was re-measured rather than trusted -- still 16 suites and 257 tests -- which mattered because the tree had since taken React 19.2.8 and lucide-react v1, a major on a UI dependency.

Corrects the staging ceiling from three to ten. Ten staging environments coexisted and the eleventh was refused, which puts these apps on Standard rather than Free. The conclusion was right for the wrong number, so only the number changed.

Records that the plan's own precondition -- resolve the staging-slot issue or thin the Renovate queue before starting -- is now met, and flags two Renovate pull requests that interact with the migration: one bumping a dependency the migration deletes, one changing the test instrument.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Documentation-only changes no longer claim a staging slot
details: Both Static Web Apps workflows deployed on every pull request regardless of what changed, so a two-file documentation change claimed a staging environment and returned nothing for it.

Filtered with paths-ignore rather than paths. An allowlist would mean enumerating every path that affects the build, and this is a single package rather than a monorepo, so there is no natural boundary to enumerate -- and anything forgotten from such a list silently skips a deploy, a considerably worse failure than one unnecessary preview. The default stays deploy; only docs, .claude and markdown are excluded.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: TypeScript majors deferred until the Vite migration
details: The TypeScript v7 pull request failed every build on an out-of-sync lockfile, but that was the symptom. It shipped a package.json bump with no lockfile at all because react-scripts@5.0.1 peer-requires typescript ^3.2.1 || ^4, so npm could not resolve v7 and Renovate's lockfile generation failed.

Nothing inside the pull request could fix that: regenerating the lockfile fails the same way, and --legacy-peer-deps would force through a real incompatibility rather than resolve it. Only the major is held; minor and patch updates continue to flow. The rule is written to be removed as part of the Vite migration, which deletes react-scripts.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: testing-library updated to jest-dom 7 and user-event 14
details: Taken deliberately before the Vite migration's first phase rather than during it, because these packages are the instrument the migration is measured with. The baseline was re-measured on top of them and still reports 16 suites and 257 tests.
The user-event 13 to 14 bump is normally the breaking one -- v14 made the API async and introduced setup() -- but no file in src imports it, so the only real risk was jest-dom 6 to 7.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Stored line endings normalised with .gitattributes
details: The repository stored 263 text files with LF and two without: one workflow with CRLF throughout and one XML example with mixed endings. Nothing declared which was intended, so a file's form depended on which tool last wrote it. Editing the CRLF workflow with a tool that writes LF turned a three-line change into a seventy-four-line diff, which is how it was noticed.

text=auto normalises the stored form. Checkout is deliberately left alone -- no eol=lf -- so core.autocrlf still decides what lands in the working tree and nobody's editor changes. Binary extensions are declared explicitly rather than left to content sniffing. The renormalisation changes no content: with carriage returns ignored, only .gitattributes itself differs.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Deploy workflows named after the environments they deploy
details: Both Static Web Apps workflows were called "Azure Static Web Apps CI/CD" and both their jobs "Build and Deploy Job". In the Actions list, in a pull request's checks, and in gh run list, a run against the production app looked identical to one against acceptance; telling them apart meant opening the run and reading which API token it used.

They now say which environment they are -- Deploy ACC and Deploy PROD, with the Azure resource name kept in parentheses. Names only: triggers, permissions, action pins and every step are untouched. Renaming a job renames the check it reports, so this was worth doing before any deploy check is ever made required.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: lucide-react updated to 1.33.0
details: A major on a UI dependency, taken in the same pass as the other majors so the Vite migration starts from a settled tree. The full suite was re-measured afterwards and still reports 16 suites and 257 tests.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Tailwind majors deferred until the Vite migration
details: Tailwind v4 fails to compile here: the PostCSS plugin moved to a separate @tailwindcss/postcss package and the configuration has to be rewritten. That is a hand migration, and it is throwaway work under Create React App, because the Vite setup replaces the PostCSS wiring with the @tailwindcss/vite plugin rather than porting it.

Left enabled, Renovate re-opens the same failing pull request every cycle and it holds a staging slot while doing so. Only the major is held. The rule is written to be removed as part of the Vite migration.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Renovate capped at five concurrent pull requests
details: Renovate's default prConcurrentLimit is ten and this configuration never overrode it. The Static Web Apps staging ceiling is also ten. The two numbers being equal meant a full Renovate queue consumed every staging environment and the next pull request opened by a human was refused outright.

That is not hypothetical: ten open dependency pull requests held all ten slots, and two unrelated pull requests had their deploy fail on arrival. It also self-perpetuated -- merging two freed two slots, and Renovate opened two new pull requests into them within the minute.

Capping at five leaves five slots permanently available for human work. Deliberately not solved by raising the tier: a higher ceiling moves the number at which the same collision happens rather than removing it.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: Node updated to v24 in the deploy workflows
details: Workflow-only change with no lockfile involvement, so nothing could invalidate it and it needed no rebase.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The supply-chain audit runs on every pull request, not only those targeting acc or main
details: The audit triggered on pull_request only for acc and main. Combined with the ruleset that makes audit a required check on acc, that produced a pull request which could never merge: one based on a feature branch matched no trigger, so it accumulated no audit at all, and because the ruleset only applies while the base is acc, GitHub reported it as CLEAN with zero checks. It read as ready and was not.

The moment its parent merged, GitHub auto-retargeted the child to acc, the ruleset began applying, the required check was missing, and the pull request blocked permanently -- a retarget emits no pull_request event, so nothing ever backfilled it.

The file already carried the argument one dimension over, in its reasoning for having no paths filter: a filter lets a pull request skip the gate by touching nothing watched, and a branches filter lets it skip by targeting a base that is not watched. push stays filtered. The deploy workflows deliberately keep their narrow filters, because an absent filter there exhausts a bounded pool of staging environments instead.

commits.subject: The Semgrep plugin's local cache is ignored

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The Create React App to Vite migration is planned
details: Create React App was deprecated on 14 February 2025. It still builds, but receives no new features, no performance work and no active security updates, which sits badly in a repository that spent August enforcing that nothing a pipeline downloads may float. linked-data-explorer already builds with Vite, so this aligns the tooling rather than introducing a third way of doing things.

Written against measurements rather than assumptions. The baseline is the existing suite, and the migration is correct when those same tests pass under Vitest and the built site behaves identically -- not "does it build", because a Vite build pointed at the wrong output directory succeeds and publishes nothing.

Scope was counted, not estimated: the env-var uses, process.env references, %PUBLIC_URL% occurrences, jest.* call sites and test scripts were each enumerated. Four phases, ordered so a working test suite exists at every point, because react-scripts provides both the build and the test runner and removing it takes away the regression net and the thing being tested at the same moment.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The release process verifies the working branch is gone from the remote
details: Merging with --delete-branch removes both copies, and the repository now deletes branches on merge, so there is normally nothing to do. But a release merged some other way leaves the remote branch behind, and one survived exactly that way and was noticed only later. Written as a check rather than an action.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The merge method is enforced by repository settings, not by remembering
details: The rule said never squash and missed that rebase-and-merge rewrites hashes just as thoroughly -- deceptively so, since it preserves the commit count while replacing every hash. Either one orphans the commit SHAs a changelog entry names.

Squash and rebase are now disabled repository-wide, leaving merge commits only, so the failure is impossible by construction rather than forbidden by a rule. GitHub's default button is "Squash and merge", so without the setting a single absent-minded click would orphan a release's entire entry.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: The config validator runs on the Node version Renovate requires
details: Renovate declares engines.node ^24.11.0 and the runner defaults to Node 22. npm accepts that mismatch with a warning rather than refusing, so the validator ran unsupported and reported green -- the kind of mismatch that keeps working right up until it abruptly does not, at which point the gate fails for a reason unrelated to anything anyone changed.

The step is placed before the audit rather than beside the validator it serves: a step following a failed one is skipped, so putting it after would mean the validator's always() condition ran on whatever Node the runner happened to default to.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: renovate.json is validated in the audit gate
details: The gate enforced that every action reference is a commit hash but had nothing to say about renovate.json, the other half of the same policy. Pinning without automated updates decays into an unpatched tree, so a Renovate that has silently stopped running is a supply-chain failure the audit is supposed to catch.

Not hypothetical: in linked-data-explorer, five keys used as JSON comments were rejected as invalid configuration and Renovate stopped opening pull requests as a precaution. Nothing in CI noticed; the repository looked green while half its policy was inert.

The validator runs as a second step in the existing audit job, so it is covered by the current required status check and needs no ruleset change. It runs with --strict, which also fails on configuration Renovate would silently auto-migrate.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Release PRs are merged, never squashed
details: The changelog entry names each commit by its SHA. Squashing a release pull request collapses them into one new commit, leaving the entry pointing at commits that do not exist on the target branch.

Renovate's dependency PRs are the opposite case and should be squashed: each is a single change, and no entry names its constituent commits. So the rule is not "never squash" but "never squash a pull request whose commits a changelog entry names".

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Releases land through a pull request
details: The acceptance branch now requires a pull request and a passing supply-chain audit, so the old flow — fast-forwarding acc locally and pushing directly — is rejected outright. Releases go through a pull request like everything else and are audited before they land.

Five further corrections came with it, all found by cutting v2026.08.2 under the new gate rather than by reasoning about it: --no-merges in the commit range, since pull-request landing puts a merge commit in every range; computing that range only after the branch is up to date, because rebasing rewrites the SHAs the entry records; a new first step reconciling open pull requests before any version editing, because dependency updates rewrite the same lockfile the version bump edits; ci added to the recognised commit types; and a rule that a source change the entry needs must be committed before the bump, or it ships unlisted.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: tailwindcss updated to 3.4.19
details: Lockfile-only dependency update raised by Renovate. It satisfied the 14-day minimum release age check and passed the supply-chain audit before merging.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: postcss updated to 8.5.23 — security advisory
details: Resolves a published security advisory in postcss.

Raised through Renovate's vulnerability-alerts path, which overrides the 14-day cooldown: this pull request carried no minimum-release-age check at all, while the tailwindcss update in the same release went through it normally.

That is the first observed confirmation that the no-cooldown security lane works end to end — GitHub advisory alerts feed Renovate, the cooldown is bypassed for them alone, and the update is still gated by the supply-chain audit before it can merge.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: CI commits get their own changelog type
details: The changelog renderer had no ci type, so pipeline and supply-chain commits fell through to the generic other icon. This release alone carries four of them, and the repo now does enough CI work for the distinction to be worth drawing.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Supply-chain gate documented, README corrected
details: Adds docs/the-gate-has-teeth.md: what the CI gate delivers, how each piece is built and why each setting is what it is, how it behaves day to day, and what it deliberately does not protect — the floating build container, npm integrity covering what is tested rather than what is shipped, and the fact that zizmor validates pin format but never pin truth.
Includes a replication guide for linked-data-explorer and ronl-business-api, and records the empty-token failure as evidence the gate works.

The README claimed the docs/ directory had been removed, which is no longer true. Product documentation still lives on the IOU Architecture site; docs/ now holds engineering records that belong beside the code.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: eslint-plugin-prettier updated to 5.5.6
details: Lockfile-only dependency update raised by Renovate, the first to land under the new policy. It passed the 14-day minimum release age check and the blocking supply-chain audit before merging.

commits.author: renovate[bot]
commits.subject: @testing-library/react updated to 16.3.2
details: Lockfile-only dependency update raised by Renovate, gated by the same 14-day cooldown and audit check. Renovate PRs are subject to the policy Renovate itself maintains.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Audit gate unblocked — the zizmor token must not be empty
details: Setting token: '' looked like sound least-privilege hardening but broke the gate outright. zizmor's --gh-token is environment-backed, and an empty value is rejected at argument parsing, before any audit runs; online-audits: false does not avoid it.

Restores the default of the workflow token, which is scoped to contents: read and mounted read-only, so the exposure this would have removed was negligible. A comment records the failure so the same hardening is not retried.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Register and spec corrected after final review
details: Renovate would have silently downgraded the deploy action. Its v1 is both a 2021 tag and a 2024 branch head; the workflows pin the branch, while Renovate resolves the tag — so a routine-looking digest update would have reverted the production deploy step to 3.5-year-old code, with the 14-day cooldown offering no protection against a years-old commit. Updates for that dependency are now disabled, with the reason recorded inline.

The register claimed blanket Renovate coverage. The zizmor version pin is an action input, which Renovate does not parse, so it never updates automatically. A Maintained-by column now separates automated pins from manual ones.

The container exception was also understated: because the build is not skipped, the production bundle is built inside the floating image, making it the build toolchain rather than merely an upload step.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Blocking supply-chain audit, Renovate cooldown and exceptions register
details: Runs zizmor on pull requests and pushes to acc and main, pinned to an exact version rather than the action default of latest — an unpinned tool inside the gate that forbids unpinned things would defeat itself. Introduced only after the tree reached zero findings, so it lands green.
Renovate maintains the digests under a 14-day cooldown, with an override so security advisories are not delayed by it.
The register records what cannot be pinned: the Static Web Apps action delegates to a container image on a floating tag, so pinning the action leaves the payload floating.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Actions pinned to digests, GITHUB_TOKEN scoped to least privilege
details: Pins actions/checkout, actions/setup-node and the Azure Static Web Apps deploy action to commit digests — all at the then-current major, so the change is behaviour-preserving rather than an upgrade.

Adds persist-credentials: false. Previously a live workflow token was written into .git/config and mounted into a closed-source third-party container; the deploy action authenticates with explicitly passed tokens instead.
Workflows now default to contents: read. The deploy job adds pull-requests: write for its PR comments; the close job takes an empty permissions block.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Hash-pin policy stated in the repository
details: Every action reference must be a commit hash, with no exemption for first-party actions. The pinned zizmor version already enforces this by default, so the file changes no findings today; it is committed so enforcement does not depend on a tool default that a future release could relax.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Implementation plan with measured checkpoints
details: Eight tasks driving the audit from 16 findings to zero, with every checkpoint count measured against the pinned zizmor version rather than estimated.

Resolves the ambiguous deploy-action reference by pinning the branch commit: the executed surface — the action manifest, its Dockerfile and its entrypoint — is byte-identical at both candidate commits, and the branch version declares a superset of inputs.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Design for supply-chain pinning of IOU pipelines
details: Records the decision to enforce hash pinning inside each repository rather than migrate to the ictu organisation, and the five-component pattern this repo pilots for linked-data-explorer and ronl-business-api.
Covers digest pins, least-privilege permissions, Renovate with a 14-day cooldown and a no-cooldown lane for advisories, a blocking audit gate, and an exceptions register.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Dangling docs/ references repointed at the documentation site
details: Earlier commits deleted the repo-side testing and namespace documentation, but references to those paths survived in the source. The IOU Architecture documentation site is now the single source of truth, so the references point at it directly rather than at paths that no longer resolve.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: bump-release no longer uses npm version, which mangles CalVer
details: npm coerces its argument to strict SemVer, and a zero-padded CalVer month is not a valid numeric identifier, so a 2026.08.x argument is silently written as 2026.8.x. There is no flag to disable the coercion. The release step now spells out editing package.json and the lockfile by hand, naming the exact keys.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: bump-release now versions the lockfile too
details: No release had ever touched package-lock.json, so it still read the value from the initial commit while package.json had moved on across 35 changelog entries. The drift was never fatal — npm ci validates dependency satisfiability rather than the root version field — but the lockfile is what CI installs from and what audit and provenance tooling reads.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Changelog tab label reverted to “Changelog”
details: `c4f4c3b` changed the tab label from `Changelog` to `Changelog!`, with a commit message reading *“chore: changelog button to changelog!”*. Nothing else in that commit touched the label and no test asserts on it, so it reads as an accidental edit that shipped rather than deliberate copy. The two changes cancel out within this release, so there is no net change for users.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Both deploys now gated on lint and the test suite
details: Neither Azure Static Web Apps workflow ran anything of this repository's own. The deploy action builds inside its own container and invokes none of our scripts, so both went from checkout straight to build-and-deploy — and with `pre-push` gating only lint and formatting, nothing anywhere stopped a deploy that broke the suite.

Both workflows now set up Node 20 and run `npm ci`, `npm run lint` and `npm run test:ci` ahead of the deploy action, with a failure blocking the deploy — covering `acc` (orange-beach) and `main` (white-sky) alike. Measured before wiring: 16 suites, 257 tests, all passing, 6.6s.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Repo-side test documentation retired in favour of the documentation site
details: Deletes `docs/TESTS.md` (333 lines) and `docs/TESTING-GUIDE.md` (188 lines). The IOU Architecture documentation site is now the single source of truth for test documentation, at `cpsv-editor/developer/testing`; the repo-side copies had drifted from what the suite actually does and are not maintained.

commits.author: Pieter 't Hoen
commits.subject: VS Code settings formatting corrected
details: Two-line formatting fix in `.vscode/settings.json`.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Prettier formatting for the Amsterdam CHANGELOG
details: Whitespace-only fix so the pre-push hook's repo-wide `check-format` passes after the prior commit's edits.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Amsterdam CHANGELOG executive summary + outputs-fallback entry
details: Adds an executive summary at the top of the Amsterdam CPRMV/DMN changelog, walking the pipeline end to end: legal analysis in iKnow, the two `HvA_full_dmn_export.dmn` iterations (with the spec-owner Q&A round in between), the deploy-blocker/FEEL fixes that landed in `HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn`, MC/DC verification, cell-level grounding, LDE validator fixes, and the CPSV Editor publish.

Also adds a changelog row documenting the DMN output-discovery gap found on republish (Concepts tab losing outputs when the live evaluate response came back empty) and its fix via `extractOutputsFromDMN`'s static XML fallback, reproduced live with a structurally-coupled input combination from the test suite.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Concepts tab lost output variables when evaluate returns no match
details: The DRD root (`hitPolicy=RULE ORDER`) has no catch-all rule, so evaluating it against the auto-generated baseline request body legitimately returns an empty result set. `extractOutputsFromTestResult()` could only discover an output's name/type from what the engine actually returned, so an empty result meant zero output concepts even though the DMN declares one. Inputs never had this problem — `generateRequestBodyFromDMN()` already reads `<dmn:inputData>` directly from the XML, independent of any evaluate result.

New `extractOutputsFromDMN()` closes the same gap for outputs: reads a decision's declared `<dmn:output>` name/type straight from the XML, namespace-agnostically, handling multiple output columns and the name-vs-label fallback. `handleEvaluateDMN` now falls back to it whenever the live evaluate result yields nothing. 7 new tests in `dmnHelpers.test.js`. Confirmed live: the Concepts tab shows the `aanspraken` output alongside the 52 inputs even when Evaluate Decision returns an empty result, and the republished TTL carries it through to TriplyDB.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: DOD met — publish Digital-Twin-Inkomensregelingen.ttl
details: Cell-level legislative grounding (Layers 1-4 of `cprmv-cell-level-linking-prototype.md`) applied to `HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn`'s Rule 1, deployed, evaluated, and published live via the CPSV Editor — zero DMN evaluation issues, zero SHACL validation issues.
Adds the published `.ttl` itself and the Gemeente Amsterdam organization logo referenced from it, plus a single consolidated CHANGELOG.md entry for the whole effort.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Cell-grounding resources weren't SHACL-conformant
details: Live SHACL validation in the CPSV Editor against a real published `.ttl` surfaced two `RuleShape` violations: `cprmv:id` is required (`sh:minCount 1`) on every `cprmv:Rule` — cell resources used `dct:identifier` instead (not checked by this shape at all), and concept resources had no identifier property whatsoever. Both now emit `cprmv:id`, including compound-cell grounding sub-resources.

`cprmv:isBasedOn` has `sh:class cprmv:Rule` — its object must itself be typed `cprmv:Rule`. Concept-resource targets already were; a direct external citation URI (CVDR, wetten.overheid.nl) was not. Every distinct citation URI referenced via `isBasedOn` now gets a minted, deduplicated stub (`<uri> a cprmv:Rule ; cprmv:id "<uri>" .`). 3 new tests; full suite passes.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Date-typed DMN inputs need type: Date, not String
details: `generateRequestBodyFromDMN()`'s `typeRef="date"` branch typed every date input as `{value: "YYYY-MM-DD", type: "String"}` on the incorrect assumption that Operaton converts internally. Wrong for any DMN that calls `.year`/`.years` on the input directly, as several Amsterdam decisions do — confirmed via Operaton's own logs (`DMN-01005 Invalid value ... for clause with type 'date'`).
Now emits the full ISO timestamp + offset with `type: 'Date'`, matching the format already documented as required elsewhere in this project's own REST variable typing notes.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Consolidate cell-grounding changelog, move notice to dmn-fix doc
details: Collapsed two same-day CHANGELOG rows into one, dropping process narrative (a CORS issue, a wrong-file mixup) already captured in the commits themselves, keeping the substance: Layers 1-4 implemented for real against `HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn`, plus the two defects building them surfaced.

`cprmv-cell-level-linking-prototype.md` trimmed to state the file choice plainly; `hva-full-dmn-export-feel-evaluation-fix.md` gains the one "Verification status" note that this file's Rule 1 carries real cell-level grounding, pointing to the prototype doc for design detail.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Ground Rule 1 in HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn, not the standalone file
details: Live-testing the deploy/evaluate CORS fix surfaced that cell-level grounding had been applied to the wrong file. `individuele inkomenstoeslag-iknow-patched.dmn` predates this project's FEEL-evaluation fix and still has 23 unfixed multi-word bare-name expressions; deploying it additionally shadowed the already-fixed decisions in `HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn` on Operaton, since both files declare identical decision keys and "latest version by key" resolution doesn't care which file a deployment came from. The stray deployment was deleted.

`HvA_full_dmn_export-patched.dmn` includes the identical decision as one of its 25 (same key, already fixed) — grounded that copy instead, with the same real citations, using its own cell ids. Redeployed as the sole source of truth; the 100-case MC/DC suite still passes 100/100, confirming the grounding attributes remain inert to FEEL evaluation as already established empirically.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Route DMN evaluate through the LDE backend too
details: Same CORS problem as the deploy fix: Evaluate Decision, "run all intermediate decisions", and "run test cases" all POSTed straight to Operaton's own evaluate endpoint from the browser, which is blocked the same way deploy was.

All three call sites now go through a shared `evaluateViaBackend()` helper hitting the LDE backend's `POST /v1/dmns/evaluate/:decisionKey`, forwarding the same request body unchanged. The "Evaluation URL" preview in the API Configuration panel now shows the actual LDE-backend URL.

commits.author: Steven Gort
commits.subject: Route DMN deploy through the LDE backend, not Operaton directly
details: Deploying straight from the browser to Operaton's `/engine-rest/deployment/create` hits CORS in local dev. `handleDeployDMN` now POSTs to the LDE backend's new `POST /v1/dmns/deploy`, mirroring the pattern `runBackendValidation()` already uses for `/v1/dmns/validate`: browser → LDE backend (CORS-allowed) → Operaton server-to-server. commits.subject: Implement cell-level legislative grounding (Layers 1-3)
details: Layer 1: `xmlns:cprmv`/`xmlns:dct` declared on `<dmn:definitions>`; real `dct:source`/`cprmv:sourceQuote`/`cprmv:isBasedOn` attributes added to Rule 1's 6 grounded cells, using citations cross-referenced from `HvA_annotaties.xml`. Confirmed to still deploy cleanly to Operaton.

Layer 2: `dmnHelpers.js`'s `extractRulesFromDMN()` now reads every cell's id, FEEL text, and groundings into `rule.inputEntries`/`outputEntries`. Surfaced a pre-existing defect: every selector-based DMN lookup silently matched nothing against a real, `dmn:`-prefixed DMN, since CSS type selectors match by (namespace, local name) and an unprefixed selector implies the null namespace — meaning cell-level grounding, and even the existing rule-level export, never actually worked for real DMN files. Fixed via a namespace-agnostic `queryAllLocal`/`queryLocal` helper.

Layer 3: `ttlGenerator.js`'s `generateDmnSection()` now emits a `cprmv:hasPart` list of per-cell `cprmv:Rule` resources on each `DecisionRule`, with deduplicated concept minting and a nested `hasPart` for compound cells. Verified end-to-end against the real DMN (11 new tests in `ttlGenerator.cellGrounding.test.js`, 2 new in `dmnHelpers.test.js`); 249/249 tests pass repo-wide.

sections.title: Test cases that expect an empty result set are now auto-verified
items: A DMN test case whose expected value is the literal empty collection "[]" (or "{}") — meaning no rule matches and the engine returns an empty result — was reported as 'OK (unchecked)' with 'the expected value could not be parsed for an automatic check'. The empty-result branch in evaluateTestCaseExpectation only recognised the descriptive strings 'empty result' / 'no matching rule', so a literal "[]" fell through to the key=value parser, found no pairs, and was judged unverified even though the engine's empty response was exactly correct.

The empty-result check now also matches a literal empty array or object, so an expected value of "[]" is treated as 'expect an empty result set'. Boundary cases such as the Thuisbatterij jaarGebondenBudget years outside the modelled range (2025, 2028) now pass automatically. A non-empty response against an "[]" expectation still fails, and structured/descriptive expectations are unaffected.

sections.title: Choose which CPRMV vocabulary version to preview, export and publish
items: A CPRMV version selector (0.4.1 / 0.3.2) next to the preview/export controls now drives the generated TTL. The editor previously always emitted the 0.4.1 namespace (https://standaarden.open-regels.nl/standards/cprmv/0.4.1#), so data published for a 0.3.x consumer was invisible to it. Selecting 0.3.2 binds cprmv: to https://cprmv.open-regels.nl/0.3.2/ — the versioned-path namespace the Linked Data Explorer /v1/norms?cprmv_version=0.3.2 query reads.

The two targets differ in shape, not just prefix. 0.4.1 wraps the rules in a cprmv:RuleSet (+ cprmv:hasPart); 0.3.2 instead emits a cprmv:Dataset / dcat:Dataset per ruleset — the unit /v1/norms reports under dataset_versions. The flat cprmv:Rule resources (cprmv:id, rulesetId, definition, situatie, norm, ruleIdPath) are emitted for both targets. Each cprmv:Dataset's dcat:version is the date that ruleset's own rules carry (from ruleIdPath), so the dataset version matches the rules' applicable_date by construction.
The selection applies consistently to the live preview, the TTL download and the publish-to-TriplyDB action.

sections.title: Consolidation date is derived from the rules, not entered by hand
items: The published consolidation date — the eli:is_realized_by version on the LegalResource and every cprmv:RuleSet's cprmv:validFrom and versioned cprmv:id — is now derived per ruleset from the BWB in-force date the rules themselves carry in their ruleIdPath (e.g. BWBR0015703_2026-04-03_0 → 2026-04-03), rather than the manually-entered 'Version or consolidation date' (eli:is_realized_by) field. That field had let an operator pick a date that disagreed with the rules — e.g. a hand-typed 2026-03-04 against 2026-04-03 rules — producing a dataset whose version never matched its rules' applicable_date.

Each ruleset is dated from its own rules, so non-primary rulesets (those entering via cprmv:Rule references, e.g. BWBR0044894 and BWBR0015711) are now versioned correctly too — previously they were emitted version-less because the editor didn't know their version, even though the rules did. The manual field remains a fallback when no rule carries a dated ruleIdPath, with today's date as a last resort.

sections.title: Rules sharing a legal path no longer collapse on publish
items: A cprmv:Rule's subject URI was built only from its ruleIdPath, so two rules on the same legal path — a range's bounds ('meer dan € 59.782, doch minder dan € 251.233') or multiple maxima ('per maand' / 'per kalenderjaar') — resolved to the same RDF subject and silently merged on publish. A 69-rule import surfaced as only 66 norms in the Linked Data Explorer.

Each rule now gets a unique subject URI: the first occurrence of a path keeps the path-derived URI, and each subsequent duplicate gets an _N suffix (_2, _3, …) in document order. Both the flat cprmv:Rule resources and the 0.4.1 cprmv:RuleSet hasPart list use the same assignment, so all values survive (69 in, 69 out). The duplicates still share a rule_id_path_key, which the LDE treats as the dedup key.
Adds a generator test for the duplicate-path case; run the suite with npm run test:generator.

sections.title: 0.3.2 datasets pass CPSV-AP 3.2.0 validation
items: The 0.3.2 cprmv:Dataset records were co-typed dcat:Dataset, which triggered the CPSV-AP 3.2.0 DatasetShape (sh:targetClass dcat:Dataset) and raised an error per dataset for missing dct:title, dct:description and dct:publisher plus an untyped dcat:landingPage. They are now typed only cprmv:Dataset — the class the Linked Data Explorer dataset_versions query reads, and one that no shape targets — so pre-publish validation passes while the data stays fully consumable. Verified against the live /v1/shacl/validate backend: 4 errors per dataset → 0. Mirrors the RuleSet emitter's existing reason for not co-typing dcat:Dataset.

sections.title: Nested sub-clauses fold into their parent rule on import
items: Importing a CPRMV Rules API payload no longer creates standalone, norm-less rules for nested enumeration sub-clauses (e.g. the 'onderdeel 1°./2°./3°.' under 'Artikel 31, lid 2, onderdeel r.'). Those hasPart members carry no rule_id_path, so they are now folded — in order, recursively — into the parent rule's cprmv:definition, which keeps the complete legal text (… ingeval: <clause> <clause> …). Nested members that are rules in their own right (carry a rule_id_path) are still imported separately. For the 1 juli 2026 0.4.1 normenbrief this turns 81 imported entries into 72 — exactly the norms /v1/norms returns.

sections.title: Toolbar polish and a runnable generator test suite
items: The CPRMV version selector is styled as a toolbar control matching the action buttons, and the Import / Show Preview / Clear All buttons no longer wrap to two lines — the header row is now a consistent height.

Generator tests are runnable with npm run test:generator (one-shot), test:generator:watch and test:ci. They cover the version selector (namespace + shape), the rules-derived dates and the duplicate-path URI handling, and live in src/utils/ttlGenerator.*.test.js so they stay in sync with the code.

sections.title: Parameter notation and label are now unconditionally required
items: validateParameter previously only required skos:notation when schema:value was also present, and never validated skos:prefLabel at all. A new cprmv:ParameterWaardeShape (added in LDE v1.9.8) makes both properties mandatory [1,n], so the client-side check now mirrors the SHACL constraint: both fields are required regardless of whether a numeric value is set.

Effect: the pre-publish validation panel in the Publish dialog and the inline form error for the Parameters tab will surface missing notation and missing label immediately, rather than letting the file through to the back-end SHACL check where the violation would only be caught on publish.

sections.title: Run test cases per decision, and gather concepts across the whole DMN
items: Run All Test Cases now routes each case to its own decision: a case's optional 'decision' field is used as the evaluation key, falling back to the selected Decision Key when absent. One test file can therefore exercise every decision of a deployed DMN — e.g. cases for jaarGebondenBudget, BerekenBeschikbaarSubsidiePlafond and RechtOpSubsidieThuisbatterij all run correctly from a single upload instead of all hitting one fixed key. Each result shows the decision it ran against.

NL-SBB concept generation now unions both inputs and outputs across every case (deduped by name), where it previously took outputs from a single result. Each variable records the decision(s) it appears in, so the Concepts tab attributes every input and output to its decision(s).

sections.title: Per-decision concept badges and persistent DMN tab
items: The Concepts tab shows a decision badge next to each variable, colour-matched to its kind: blue beside Input #x (inputs are DRD-level and may belong to several decisions) and green beside Output #x. Output concepts are clustered so variables from the same decision sit together, without separate group headers. The DMN tab's test-case decision badges match the blue Input styling.

The DMN tab now keeps its state when switching tabs: an uploaded DMN, deployment status and the full test-case run results survive a hop to the Concepts tab and back, instead of being reset each time the tab unmounted.

sections.title: Pick which decision to evaluate in multi-decision DMNs
items: extractPrimaryDecisionKey now prefers a *root* decision — one that no other decision requires via informationRequirement/requiredDecision — instead of blindly taking the first <decision> element in document order. This fixes models where the intended output decision is authored later in the file. When a DMN has several independent roots (e.g. a combined Recht-én-Hoogte model), document order still breaks the tie and a console warning points to the picker.

The DMN File card now shows a Decision Key dropdown whenever a file contains more than one testable decision, listing each as 'Name (id)'. Selecting one updates the Decision Key and the evaluation URL everywhere — so e.g. RechtOpSubsidieThuisbatterij can be chosen even though BehaalbareHoogteSubsidie appears first.

sections.title: Test cases now verify functional correctness, not just a 200
items: Previously a test case went green whenever the HTTP call succeeded, regardless of the returned values. A new evaluateTestCaseExpectation compares each case's expected outputs against the engine's actual outputs and returns PASS, FAIL, or unverified. It parses the readable 'key=value, reden="…"' expected strings, accepts a structured expected object, and special-cases the 'empty result set' expectation.

Results render PASS (green), FAIL (red, with an Expected-vs-Actual mismatch table per output), ERROR (red, when the call itself fails) and OK-unchecked (amber, when no expectation could be parsed — never a silent green). The summary and header counts are now verdict-based, so 'N/N passed' means functionally correct results.

sections.title: Imported DMNs now SHACL-conformant too
items: Imported DMN blocks are preserved verbatim, so their Decision Rules bypassed the v1.10.0 CPSV-AP fixes and still failed validation (missing dct:title/dct:description, cpsv:implements pointing at the PublicService). generateDmnSection now runs a normalizeImportedDmnBlocks pass over the preserved blocks: each cpsv:Rule gets dct:title and dct:description injected when absent, and a cpsv:implements that points at a /services/ URI is repointed to the eli:LegalResource (or dropped when no legal resource exists).

Edits are additive/repointing only — no preserved DMN triples are removed — and idempotent, so re-importing an already-conformant export is a no-op. Verified: a re-imported DMN with non-conformant decision rules validates clean against both CPSV-AP 3.2.0 and CPRMV 0.4.1.

sections.title: Valid, readable IRIs for NL-SBB concept URIs
items: Generated concept URIs containing spaces (e.g. .../concepts/behaalbarehoogtesubsidie/Reeds gesubsidieerd eigenaren) produced invalid Turtle — the lenient importer round-tripped them but the strict (SHACL) parser failed with 'Unexpected <…> on line N'. A shared sanitizeIri helper now replaces whitespace with underscores (…/Reeds_gesubsidieerd_eigenaren) and percent-encodes the few remaining IRI-illegal characters, applied to the concept URI, dct:subject and skos:exactMatch. Underscores are valid and idempotent, so a downloaded .ttl re-imports cleanly.

Concept URIs and skos:exactMatch are now built URI-safe at the source: DMN-extracted concepts sanitize the variable name, and the Concepts tab 'Variable Name (used in URI)' input now enforces no spaces (converted to underscores) instead of only hinting at it.

Existing skos:exactMatch values under the .../concepts/ namespace also have hyphens converted to underscores so they match the underscore-style concept URIs (e.g. .../concepts/Reeds-gesubsidieerd-eigenaren → .../concepts/Reeds_gesubsidieerd_eigenaren); external exactMatch links on other domains are left untouched.

sections.title: Populate the Concepts tab from test cases too
items: Running uploaded test cases now fills the Concepts tab even without a manual evaluate: input concepts are derived from the union of every uploaded case's request-body variables (so all inputs across all cases are covered, not just one case), which needs no successful evaluate; output concepts are still added from the last successful result when there is one.

sections.title: Round-trip dct:spatial on import
items: Import now reads the organisation's spatial value from both dct:spatial (the current CPSV-AP output) and cv:spatial (legacy files). Previously the importer only read cv:spatial, so a downloaded file — which emits dct:spatial — lost the value on re-import and re-generated without it, causing a 'Less than 1 values … dct:spatial' CPSV-AP error on the second pass. Downloaded files now re-import and re-validate cleanly.

sections.title: Clarify pre-publish SHACL validation scope
items: PublishDialog's pre-publish SHACL panel now explains it checks the Turtle that will actually be published — the editor's current (regenerated) output — which can differ from an originally-imported file, since import normalizes legacy CPRMV/CPSV-AP terms to the CPRMV 0.4.1 / CPSV-AP 3.2.0 vocabulary. An imported file that fails validation on its own may still publish as conformant

sections.title: CPRMV 0.4.1 conformance
items: cprmv: namespace bumped from https://cprmv.open-regels.nl/0.3.0/ to the canonical https://standaarden.open-regels.nl/standards/cprmv/0.4.1# (constants.js TTL_NAMESPACES + vocabularies.config.js), and a prov: prefix added; vocabulary config gains cprmv:RuleSet / cprmv:RuleMethod entity types with detection ordered before cprmv:Rule (since 'a cprmv:Rule' is a substring of 'a cprmv:RuleSet')

ttlGenerator now emits a 0.4.1-conformant cprmv:RuleSet per rulesetId — replacing the old cprmv:Dataset section — carrying the RuleSetShape-required cprmv:id, cprmv:validFrom^^xsd:date (from the legal resource date, else today), cprmv:isOutputOf → the cpsv:PublicService, cprmv:hasMethod → a dual-typed cprmv:RuleMethod, cprmv:CodificationMethod node, an ordered cprmv:hasPart RDF list of its Rules, and a prov:wasDerivedFrom link to the legal source
Every cprmv:Rule now always emits cprmv:id (required by RuleShape); cprmv:extends renamed to cprmv:isBasedOn in the temporal/decision sections
Verified: an editor-generated TTL (example import → full generator) validates clean against the CPRMV 0.4.1 SHACL shapes (0 violations)

sections.title: Import the CPRMV 0.4.1 API output
items: New src/utils/cprmvImport.js flattenCprmvRules walks the CPRMV Rules API shape (array of cprmv:RuleSet objects with nested …#hasPart object-maps), recursing and flattening sub-rules into the editor's flat rule model, with nested rules inheriting their parent rulesetId

Reads the 0.4.1 standards keys plus the http://cprmv.open-regels.nl/ extension predicates (situatie/norm/rulesetid/rule_id_path), and tolerates legacy 0.4.1-slash and 0.3.0 keys and flat-array exports
handleImportJSON (App.js) and CPRMVTab 'Load Example' both use the shared flattener; the bundled cprmv-example.json is replaced with the conformant API output

sections.title: CPSV-AP 3.2.0 conformance
items: Service: dct:language and cv:sector (and cv:thematicArea) references are now typed in-graph (dct:LinguisticSystem / skos:Concept) so the file-local SHACL sh:class checks pass without entailment
Organisation: emits dct:spatial (was the non-conformant cv:spatial) pointing at a dct:Location-typed node, satisfying PublicOrganisationShape

cpsv:Rule nodes (Temporal Rules and DMN Decision Rules) now always emit the required dct:identifier, dct:title@nl and dct:description@nl, and cpsv:implements points at the eli:LegalResource (not the PublicService) — or is omitted when no legal resource is set

Verified: a full editor-generated TTL (service + organisation + temporal rule + DMN decision rules + CPRMV rules) validates clean against both the CPSV-AP 3.2.0 and CPRMV 0.4.1 SHACL shapes (0 violations on each)

sections.title: Pre-publish SHACL validation (advisory)
items: New src/utils/shaclHelper.js validateTtl POSTs the generated Turtle to REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL/v1/shacl/validate and returns the layered result; it never throws — an unreachable backend yields a neutral { unavailable: true } shape (mirroring DMNTab.runBackendValidation)

PublishDialog runs validation when it opens (and via a 'Validate now' button) and renders a layered CPRMV / CPSV-AP / RONL result panel with per-layer issues; it is purely advisory and never blocks publishing, with a distinct amber state when the backend is unreachable

DMN tab is prefilled with fileName decision-{dmnId}.dmn, the fetched XML, and the primary decision key, while staying fully interactive (isImported stays false, so deploy/test/publish run through the existing DMNTab + PublishDialog flow rather than the imported-preserved mode)

Service tab is prefilled from the DSO activity (dct:title from activityName, dct:identifier from activityUrn, and a Dutch provenance description carrying activityUrn + fsRef); Organization tab is prefilled from the resolved authority (skos:prefLabel + dct:identifier)

After consuming the link the import params are stripped via history.replaceState so a refresh can't re-import, and a consumedRef guard prevents StrictMode double-invoke; status is reported through the existing message banner

sections.title: Shared decision-key extraction + external-content hydration
items: extractPrimaryDecisionKey lifted out of DMNTab.jsx into src/utils/dmnHelpers.js and exported, so the import hook and the DMN tab share one implementation (skips p_* constants, falls back to the first decision) instead of duplicating the parser

DMNTab now hydrates its internal uploadedFile / decisionKey / test body / parsed decisions / syntactic validation from dmnData.content whenever content arrives from outside the tab (e.g. the DSO deep-link) and no file was uploaded locally — without this, deploy and test stayed gated on the internal uploadedFile state and an imported DMN appeared unusable

sections.title: Request body generation reads <inputValues> constraints
items: generateRequestBodyFromDMN in DMNTab.jsx now checks every decisionTable input column for an <inputValues> FEEL list whose inputExpression matches an inputData name, and uses the first allowed value as the starter — DMNs that constrain string inputs (e.g. norm descriptions, status codes) no longer produce empty values that would fail at Operaton evaluate time

Two helper closures added: parseFirstFeelListItem (unwraps quoted strings, coerces booleans, parses numbers from a FEEL comma-separated list) and findInputValuesExample (scans decisionTable inputs for a matching constraint)

Fallback path unchanged: inputData without a corresponding inputValues constraint continues to flow through the existing typeRef switch and name-based heuristics (datum/date → today, geboorte → random adult birth date, aantal/bedrag/inkomen → 0, etc.), so every existing project DMN keeps generating the same starter body as before

sections.title: Surface unreachable validation backend

parseError bubble styling now adapts to the unavailable case — amber instead of red — matching the meaning of the message

sections.title: cprmv:Dataset generation
items: TTL export now emits a cprmv:Dataset block per unique cprmv:rulesetId across the CPRMV Rules collection — one Dataset per legal source, dual-typed cprmv:Dataset and dcat:Dataset for DCAT catalogue interop

Dataset properties: dct:identifier, dct:title (primary only), cprmv:rulesetId, cprmv:implements (versioned for primary, un-versioned for non-primary), dcat:version (primary only), dct:issued, dcat:landingPage

New buildLegalUriForRulesetId() helper handles BWB, CVDR, and full-URI inputs; defensively strips /YYYY-MM-DD[/N] from already-versioned inputs before appending the version, eliminating doubled-version URIs
